stories.title: Boston Dynamics unveils Stretch Gen 2 trailer-unloading robot
paragraphs: The Robot Report says Boston Dynamics unveiled Stretch Gen 2, the next generation of its autonomous mobile trailer-unloading robot, citing more than 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of boxes handled with the earlier model. Vice president Brian Donnelly told the outlet the company spent about two and a half years simplifying and hardening the design for uptime and serviceability.

According to The Robot Report, Stretch Gen 2 can unload up to 1,000 cases per hour depending on case weight and stacking, with a multipick gripper, a battery rated for two shifts, and a fast charger that reaches about 90% in roughly 75 minutes. The redesign cuts about 81% of internal cabling (around half a mile), adds automotive-grade connectors, continuous-rotation joints past 360°, recessed emergency stop hardware, and sturdier exterior panels.

Donnelly said a full swerve-drive swap now takes about one hour instead of a full day, and new onboard diagnostics push more routine service to customer teams. The Robot Report notes Stretch Gen 2 is already running at multiple customer sites, with software updates rolling out roughly monthly; a recent fleet update raised unload rates by about 24%, per Donnelly.

stories.title: Physicl raises $10M seed to build high-fidelity 3D worlds for robot training
paragraphs: TechCrunch reports that Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to help world-model designers and robot builders train on more realistic simulations. Founder and CEO Alex de Vigan previously built nfinite for e-commerce 3D product renderings.

According to TechCrunch, Physicl is releasing Studio with 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets so users can build scenes that generate synthetic data for edge cases such as a cup on a cluttered or shadowed counter. Early customer SpAItial used the data to improve fidelity for its Echo-3 world-model product.

de Vigan told TechCrunch the company aims to turn unstructured real-world inputs into high-fidelity geometry, materials, and physics for ongoing synthetic-data generation, not only one-off datasets. SpAItial CEO Matthias Niessner described on-the-fly data generation during training as especially attractive.
